name: Shrug
pattern: Shoulder blade elevation: arms hang straight while the shoulders lift straight up toward the ears and lower.
setup: Stand tall, weights at your sides or bar in front of the thighs.
Arms straight and relaxed, grip just outside the hips.
Chin level, neck long, brace your trunk.

steps.text: Lift your shoulders straight up toward your ears.
Hold for a second at the top.
Lower slowly until the shoulders are fully down and stretched.

cues.cue: Straight up and straight down, no rolling.
cues.why: The upper trap and levator lift the shoulder blade; rolling adds no work and strains the shoulder.

cues.cue: Arms stay straight, do not bend the elbows.
cues.why: Bending the elbows turns it into a row or curl.

cues.cue: Try arms slightly out to the sides (about 30°).
cues.why: Shrugging with the arms abducted 30° raised upper, middle and lower trapezius and serratus activity versus arms at the sides.

cues.cue: Chin level, do not push the head forward.
cues.why: A jutting head loads the neck instead of the traps.

cues.cue: Full range: stretch at the bottom, ears at the top.
cues.why: The shrug is the highest upper-trapezius exercise when done through full range.

breathing: Breathe out as you lift, in as you lower.

tempo.note: Lift in 1 s, hold 1 s, lower in 2 s.

mistakes.name: Rolling the shoulders
mistakes.looks: Shoulders circle forward or back at the top.
mistakes.why: It adds no muscle work and can irritate the shoulder.

mistakes.name: Head pokes forward
mistakes.looks: The chin juts out as you lift.
mistakes.fix: Keep your chin tucked and level.
mistakes.why: Loads the neck joints and turns the move into a neck strain.

mistakes.name: Elbows bend
mistakes.looks: Elbows bend and the weight is pulled up with the arms.
mistakes.fix: Relax the arms, use straps if grip fails.
mistakes.why: The biceps and deltoids help and the traps do less.

mistakes.name: Tiny range
mistakes.looks: Shoulders barely move with a very heavy load.
mistakes.fix: Use a weight you can lift to your ears.
mistakes.why: The trap gets most of its work through full elevation.

safety: Neck pain: lighter weight, slower reps, chin level.
Heavy loads: use straps and keep the back straight when picking up the weight.

variants.change: Bar behind the thighs: shoulders slightly back, a bit more mid-trap.
On a bench: no leg help, different angle of pull.
Trap bar: handles at your sides, neutral grip.
Arms wider: more upward rotation; more lower trapezius and serratus.
Power shrug: small hip and knee dip then a fast shrug, like the top of a clean.
Gripless machine: pads on the shoulders, grip does not limit you.
One side: do not lean away.

subtypes.name: Overhead shrug
subtypes.change: Arms locked overhead (or upside down on the hands): push up tall to lift the shoulders toward the ears, then let them sink.

subtypes.name: Scapular retraction
subtypes.change: Seated or lying, arms straight in front: pull the shoulder blades together, then let them spread; arms do not bend.

motion.basis: Muscle roles from ekstrom2003 (shrug gives the highest upper-trapezius activity) and pizzari2014 (shrug at 30° abduction recruits the upward rotators). Scapular elevation values are on the app's -1..+1 scale and are estimates; a small upward rotation with elevation is an estimate. No kinematic study of the loaded shrug was found.

sources.cite: Ekstrom RA, Donatelli RA, Soderberg GL. Surface electromyographic analysis of exercises for the trapezius and serratus anterior muscles. J Orthop Sports Phys Ther. 2003;33(5):247-258.
Pizzari T, Wickham J, Balster S, Ganderton C, Watson L. Modifying a shrug exercise can facilitate the upward rotator muscles of the scapula. Clin Biomech. 2014;29(2):201-205.
Haff GG, Triplett NT, eds. Essentials of Strength Training and Conditioning. 4th ed. National Strength and Conditioning Association. Human Kinetics; 2016.
